**(1) First message**

```text
gauntlet: question
The framing holds: checked the gather draft's recon of the reports page render path, which shows a table with no export action. Checked the table column definitions as consumed by src/export/csv.ts, the existing CSV serializer, and the paging path the 10k-row export would run through. Checked the 10k-row verification's implicit dependencies on a 10k-row fixture and a timing harness. I ran no tools this turn, so these checks rest on the draft's citations and not on a fresh read of primary code.

Supported premises, all from the gather draft:
- The reports page has no export action today.
- The table's column definitions can drive an export, since src/export/csv.ts already reuses them.
- A CSV serializer exists to reuse.

Unverified premises:
- The draft says paging supports the 10k-row, under-60s target. That is a performance claim. No measurement is cited, and neither the repo nor the ticket names a benchmark command. I carry it as an assumption into Open Questions.
- The 10k-row acceptance check also depends on a 10k-row report fixture and a way to time the export. The draft names neither, and no lookup was available to confirm one exists. I treat this as unverified and carry it into `## Problem`.

Assumption: ticket acme/widgets#77 groups rows by repo. This repo is acme/widgets, per the overrides `## Issue tracker` setting. So the three acme/widgets rows are `in-scope`. The acme/mailer row, "Exports are emailed to the requesting user.", is `elsewhere: acme/mailer` and creates no work here.

Where should the Export CSV button appear on the reports page?
A) beside the report title
B) in a toolbar directly above the table
C) in the table footer next to the pager
D) other - name it
Recommendation: A - the title area is the page-level action spot, so the button reads as exporting the whole report and not just the current page.
```

**(2) Approaches message**

```text
gauntlet: question
Before the approaches, here are the two implicit dependencies I could not check.

- The 10k-row, under-60s acceptance check needs a 10k-row report fixture. I looked for one in the gather draft, the ticket, and the overrides. None names a fixture, so this is unverified.
- The same check needs a timing harness or benchmark command. I looked in the same places and found none. This is also unverified.

The spec will name both as test setup to create, and the 60s target stays an Open Question until a measurement exists.

The axis separating the options is where the CSV gets assembled: in the reports page from paged fetches, or on the server behind a new endpoint.

I recommend A, the reuse-only option. Clicking an Export CSV button beside the report title would:
- walk the existing paging to fetch every page of the report;
- pass the rows and the visible table columns, in table order, to the existing serializer in src/export/csv.ts;
- trigger a file download.

This adds no new export construct. The serializer already reads the table's column definitions, so "every column shown in the table" comes from the same source the table renders from. The trade-off is that a 10k-row export runs as many sequential page fetches in the browser. That is the unmeasured part of the 60s target.
Removes: none
Adds: Export CSV button in the reports page header beside the title; click handler that pages through the report and calls src/export/csv.ts with the visible columns in table order; download trigger; reports-page export test file; 10k-row fixture and timing test
Pattern: follows src/export/csv.ts, which already reuses the table's column definitions, so there is one column source and one serializer.

B drops the ask's implicit assumption that the export is built where the table is shown. A new server endpoint would generate the whole CSV and return it as one download. The server would still call the same serializer, and the button would just request the endpoint. This avoids per-page round trips from the browser and is more likely to hold the 60s target as reports grow. The cost is a new route and a server-side copy of the visible column selection that must stay in step with the table.
Removes: none
Adds: export endpoint and route; server-side call to src/export/csv.ts; column selection passed from the page to the endpoint; Export CSV button beside the title calling it; endpoint test file; 10k-row fixture and timing test
Pattern: reuses src/export/csv.ts but adds a second place that decides which columns are visible, beside the table's own column definitions.

The emailed-export variant is not considered here because that row is elsewhere: acme/mailer.

What would flip the recommendation: if the 10k-row timing test shows the paged browser export exceeding 60s, B becomes the recommendation.

Which approach should the design use?
A) reuse-only: page through and serialize in the reports page with the existing serializer and paging
B) server endpoint that builds the CSV with the same serializer
C) other - name it
Recommendation: A - it meets every in-scope row with no new construct and one column source, pending the 10k-row measurement.
```

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
### 1. First message

gauntlet: question
The gathered draft reports that the reports page has no export action and that `src/export/csv.ts` can reuse the table’s column definitions. Those findings support adding export through the existing CSV path, but I cannot independently verify the framing: no tools or primary code observations are available here. In particular, the serializer’s callers, visible-column ordering, paging’s full-report traversal, and the claimed 10k-row performance capability remain unverified.

The ticket requires a button, every displayed column, and export of 10k rows in under 60 seconds. I’ll interpret “every column shown” as the visible table columns in table order, consistent with your recorded answer. The `acme/mailer` email criterion belongs to a known nonmember repository and receives `elsewhere: acme/mailer`; it does not add email delivery to this implementation.

Where should the Export CSV button appear?
A) Beside the report title.
B) In the table toolbar.
C) Other — name the location.
Recommendation: A - it matches your recorded placement decision and makes export a report-level action.

### 2. Approaches message

Your recorded answers settle the placement beside the report title, visible columns in table order, and reuse of the existing CSV serializer and paging.

Before comparing approaches, the remaining dependencies need explicit qualification. The draft identifies `src/export/csv.ts`, but its exports, callers, and treatment of visible-column order have not been independently inspected; no lookup was possible without tools. The paging implementation’s ability to retrieve the complete report rather than only the displayed page is likewise unverified. Finally, the draft’s performance claim is not accompanied by a measurement: completing a 10k-row export in under 60 seconds remains an acceptance requirement, not an established capability.

**I recommend the reuse-only approach**, consistent with your recorded choice. The distinguishing axis is whether export remains in the existing reports-page execution path or gains a separate execution boundary.

**A) Reuse the existing CSV serializer and paging.** Add the button beside the title, obtain visible columns in table order from the table’s owning definitions, retrieve the full report through existing paging, and serialize through `src/export/csv.ts`. If that shared serializer nearly fits but lacks ordered-column selection, extend its existing interface rather than copying it beside the page.

This introduces the fewest moving parts. Its risks are incomplete page traversal, UI responsiveness, and changes affecting existing serializer callers. Those callers need inspection before deciding whether its interface needs modification.

Removes: None.
Adds: Report-title export button and handler; full-report export orchestration using existing paging; an ordered-column parameter on the existing serializer only if needed; export correctness, paging, and performance tests.
Pattern: Follows the draft-reported shared-column reuse in `src/export/csv.ts`; preserves one serialization path rather than duplicating it.

**B) Reuse the same serializer and paging behind a browser worker.** This alternative drops the assumption that export must execute on the page’s main thread. The button and column contract remain unchanged, but export work crosses a worker boundary.

It could improve responsiveness during large exports, at the cost of worker messaging, data transfer, and error propagation. It is only viable if the existing serializer and paging dependencies can run in a worker; that compatibility is not established by the supplied observations. It also does not by itself prove the under-60-second requirement.

Removes: None.
Adds: The same button, ordered-column contract, and full-report orchestration; worker entry point and message contract; worker lifecycle and failure handling; corresponding correctness and performance tests.
Pattern: Retains the shared serializer identified at `src/export/csv.ts`, but adds an isolation boundary whose necessity is not yet demonstrated.

I would switch from A to B only if inspection establishes worker compatibility and representative measurement shows that the direct reuse path causes unacceptable UI blocking. Neither alternative changes the ticket’s column or performance requirements, or takes ownership of email delivery.
